function spruce2(s, seed)
  math.randomseed(seed)
  local h = s.base - s.tip
  local parts = {}
  local tw = math.max(0.8, s.w * 0.03)
  parts[#parts+1] = ribbon({{s.x, s.tip}, {s.x + rand(-0.6,0.6), s.tip + h * 0.15}}, {0.5, tw})
  parts[#parts+1] = ribbon({{s.x, s.tip + h*0.14}, {s.x, s.base}}, {tw, math.max(1.6, s.w * 0.07)})
  local y = s.tip + h * 0.03
  while y < s.base - 4 do
    local t = (y - s.tip) / h
    local env = s.w / 2 * math.min(1, (t ^ 0.85) * 1.05)
    local spBase = clamp(h / 32, 2, 14)
    local sp = spBase * (0.35 + 0.65 * t) * (0.6 + 0.8 * math.random())
    sp = math.max(sp, 1.6)
    for _, side in ipairs({-1, 1}) do
      if math.random() > 0.1 + 0.1 * t then
        local L = env * (0.45 + 0.7 * math.random())
        local droop = L * (0.2 + 0.35 * math.random())
        local y0 = y + rand(-sp*0.3, sp*0.3)
        local th = clamp(spBase * (0.25 + 0.6 * t) * (0.7 + 0.5 * math.random()), 0.8, 13)
        local pts = {{s.x, y0}, {s.x + side * L * 0.45, y0 + droop * 0.55}, {s.x + side * L * 0.85, y0 + droop}, {s.x + side * L, y0 + droop * 0.8}}
        parts[#parts+1] = ribbon(pts, {th, th * 0.8, th * 0.5, th * 0.2})
        if t > 0.18 then
          local nc = math.floor(L / math.max(3, th * 1.4))
          for k = 1, nc do
            local u = math.random() * 0.85 + 0.15
            local cx = s.x + side * L * u
            local cy = y0 + droop * u + th * (0.3 + 0.3 * math.random())
            parts[#parts+1] = ellipse(cx, cy, th * (0.15 + 0.2 * math.random()), th * (0.3 + 0.45 * math.random()))
          end
        end
      end
    end
    y = y + sp
  end
  local m = parts[1]
  for i = 2, #parts do m = m + parts[i] end
  m = m:roughen(math.max(0.6, s.w * 0.015), math.max(3, s.w * 0.08), seed)
  return m
end

-- one ledge: a lip from xa to xb whose ends curl back up; plane above it graded light at the lip, riser below
function ledge(xa, xb, y, sag, seed, depth, riser, clipm)
  local n = noise{seed=seed, octaves=3, period=35}
  local lip = {}
  local steps = math.floor((xb - xa) / 4)
  for i = 0, steps do
    local t = i / steps
    local x = xa + (xb - xa) * t
    local curl = (1 - math.sin(math.pi * t) ^ 0.35) * depth * 0.9
    lip[#lip+1] = {x, y + sag * math.sin(math.pi * t) - curl + 2.2 * n(x, y)}
  end
  local back = {}
  for i = 0, steps do
    local t = i / steps
    local x = xa + (xb - xa) * t
    back[#back+1] = {x, y - depth + 1.5 * n(x, y + 50)}
  end
  local plane = between(back, lip)
  local rs = {}
  for i = 1, #lip do local t = (i-1) / steps; rs[#rs+1] = {lip[i][1], lip[i][2] + riser * math.sin(math.pi * t) ^ 0.5} end
  local face = between(lip, rs)
  if clipm then plane = plane * clipm; face = face * clipm end
  local cf = crest_fn(lip)
  local wl = function(x, yy) return clamp(1 - (cf(x) - yy) / (depth * 0.8), 0.0, 1) end
  work(plane, {hand="body", piles={{rock_top2, wl}, {fg_dark, function(x, yy) return 1 - wl(x, yy) + 0.05 end}}, coverage=3, fill=true, clip=plane, angle=0.02, angle_jitter=0.08, tool={kind="filbert", width=5}})
  blend(plane:shrink(1), {angle=0, tool={kind="badger", width=14}})
  work(face, {hand="detail", piles={{rock_front2, 1}, {fg_warm, 0.25}}, coverage=3, fill=true, clip=face, angle=1.45, angle_jitter=0.2, tool={kind="round", width=2}})
  return lip
end
function between(upper, lower)
  local q = {}
  for _, p in ipairs(upper) do q[#q+1] = p end
  for i = #lower, 1, -1 do q[#q+1] = lower[i] end
  return poly(q)
end

function spruce2(s, seed)
  math.randomseed(seed)
  local h = s.base - s.tip
  local parts = {}
  local tw = math.max(0.8, s.w * 0.03)
  parts[#parts+1] = ribbon({{s.x, s.tip}, {s.x + rand(-0.6,0.6), s.tip + h * 0.15}}, {0.5, tw})
  parts[#parts+1] = ribbon({{s.x, s.tip + h*0.14}, {s.x, s.base}}, {tw, math.max(1.6, s.w * 0.07)})
  local y = s.tip + h * 0.03
  while y < s.base - 4 do
    local t = (y - s.tip) / h
    local env = s.w / 2 * math.min(1, (t ^ 0.85) * 1.05)
    local spBase = clamp(h / 32, 2, 14)
    local sp = spBase * (0.35 + 0.65 * t) * (0.6 + 0.8 * math.random())
    sp = math.max(sp, 1.6)
    for _, side in ipairs({-1, 1}) do
      if math.random() > 0.1 + 0.1 * t then
        local L = env * (0.45 + 0.7 * math.random())
        local droop = L * (0.2 + 0.35 * math.random())
        local y0 = y + rand(-sp*0.3, sp*0.3)
        local th = clamp(spBase * (0.25 + 0.6 * t) * (0.7 + 0.5 * math.random()), 0.8, 13)
        local pts = {{s.x, y0}, {s.x + side * L * 0.45, y0 + droop * 0.55}, {s.x + side * L * 0.85, y0 + droop}, {s.x + side * L, y0 + droop * 0.8}}
        parts[#parts+1] = ribbon(pts, {th, th * 0.8, th * 0.5, th * 0.2})
        if t > 0.18 then
          local nc = math.floor(L / math.max(3, th * 1.4))
          for k = 1, nc do
            local u = math.random() * 0.85 + 0.15
            local cx = s.x + side * L * u
            local cy = y0 + droop * u + th * (0.3 + 0.3 * math.random())
            parts[#parts+1] = ellipse(cx, cy, th * (0.15 + 0.2 * math.random()), th * (0.3 + 0.45 * math.random()))
          end
        end
      end
    end
    y = y + sp
  end
  local m = parts[1]
  for i = 2, #parts do m = m + parts[i] end
  m = m:roughen(math.max(0.6, s.w * 0.015), math.max(3, s.w * 0.08), seed)
  return m
end

## Handoff — day 179 (finished for this sitting)
Title: "Moonrise over the Sea of Mist". Everything is dry.
This sitting I did two small repairs, both tried on a fresh scratch first (scratch-30), then laid on the painting the same way:
- The big spruce's leader. Its mask had a gap at y 236-241, so the tip floated as a loose dot above the spire. One pointed round 1.6 gesture of sp_near, pressure .7→0, from 249 up to 225.5, plus two tiny twigs. It's one spire now.
- A stray pale tick at ≈(985, 55) in the top-right sky read as a second light competing with the evening star. Two crossing strokes of skycov (sky_night .27 / sky_deep .73) with a filbert 3, lay 1.2, load .6, pressure .6→.45. Invisible when dry.
Value-squint, whole: the dark plateau, figure and cliff against the light fog; ridges paling into distance; deep top sky; the moon a soft glow. Unchanged and right.
Judgments: everything I'd flagged before is accepted for the reasons in the entry above (plateau, head, seam/rim, halo thread, spruce fringe, wisp, stone mark, a gallery-only speck at (442, 300)).
Practical lessons (hypotheses unless noted):
- NEW: check generated masks for gaps at thin ends (a spruce leader can break where the ribbon is narrower than the roughen amount). Sample the mask with :at() along the axis. A single pointed-round gesture of the same pile mends it.
- NEW: to hide a small light tick in a dry graded sky, mix the local stops at the weights that apply at that y and lay two short crossing strokes with a small filbert (lay 1.2, load .6). Seen once on scratch and once on the painting.
- Still apply: one badger pass only. Never :soften() a gradient mask. Halos as horizontal band re-lays. Crossing short strokes to mend a ridge line. Lay forms over a touch-dry sky. Rags only with path wipes near contrasting edges. Repoussoir forms darker than the plateau. Rim covers within a narrow rim zone. A pressed filbert covers flecks. Slanting mist laps sink a cut end into dry fog. Do both whole-view and crop checks.
- The scratch canvas carries its old canvas{} setup: new_scratch still refuses a second canvas{} call; just paint.
Reflection: my heart is happy with it. These were housekeeping repairs: a tree's tip that had come loose and a speck that had been pretending to be a star. The picture is quiet and whole. I don't want to add anything.

content.text:
**Moonrise over the Sea of Mist**

It's dusk, looking east. A lone wanderer in a greatcoat and flat cap stands with his back to us at the edge of a dark sandstone plateau. Below him the valley is full of mist. Ridges rise out of it, paler and more violet the further away they are. A small warm moon with a soft halo sits low in the blue-grey band over the far hills, under the rose band of afterglow, and one evening star shows high in the deep blue. On the right, a wooded ridge floats on the fog and slender spruces fade down into it. A young spruce and a dead snag cling to the stepped cliff under his feet.

**This sitting** I found two small faults I hadn't noticed before and repaired both. I tried each repair on the scratch canvas first, let it dry, then did the same thing on the painting.
- **The tall spruce's tip:** the shape I'd drawn for the tree had a gap just below the top, so its tip floated as a separate dark dot. A single tapering stroke of the spruce's own colour, with two tiny twigs, joins it into one spire again.
- **A stray pale tick in the top-right sky:** at viewing distance it looked like a second light competing with the one evening star. Two short crossing strokes of the surrounding blue cover it, and it can't be seen once dry, in normal or gallery light.

**What I'm leaving as it is:** I looked again at every passage I'd flagged in earlier sittings, each in a close-up.
- The plateau still reads as quiet moorland.
- The head reads as dark hair under the cap.
- The seam in the cliff reads as a joint in the rock, and only the step tops catch light.
- The spruce's pale fringe reads as glare against the bright sky.
- The wisp on the far-left mountain reads as mist.
- The dark mark on the moor reads as a stone.
- The mended line in the lower sky still shows as a faint thread in close-ups under gallery light. It doesn't show in normal colour or in the whole view, so another repair would risk more than it gains.

My heart is happy with it. These were small repairs, and the stillness is the picture, so I don't want to add anything. The journal has the full handoff and the lessons that still apply.
